name: Two-sided grid, 5-minute BTC
one_liner: The same two-sided net grid on 5-minute data, with a stricter storm filter and only 2 nets per side. Does the small grid edge survive on the fast, expensive 5-minute timeframe?
how_it_works: The same fishing-nets idea as the 1-hour version: nets above (sell) and below (buy) the price, capturing bounces. But on 5-minute data price crosses nets far more often, so there are fewer nets (2 per side) and the storm filter is stricter (needs 0.8% drift instead of 0.5%).

params.name: Spacing between orders
params.plain: 1.5× the typical swing of one 5-minute candle.
params.why: Same 'not too tight, not too wide' rule as the 1-hour version.

params.name: How many orders
params.plain: 2 buy orders below the price and 2 sell orders above.
params.why: Fewer nets than on 1-hour data on purpose: 5-minute price crosses nets very often, and every crossing pays a fee.

params.name: When it re-arms
params.plain: Every 96 five-minute candles (8 hours), the nets move to surround the current price.
params.why: Keeps the nets near the fish, as always.

params.name: Only in calm markets (the weather check)
params.plain: Compares the average price of the last 50 candles with the last 100. If they drift apart more than 0.8%, it declares a trend and closes everything; it only returns below 0.2%.
params.why: Stricter than the 1-hour version because 5-minute noise is worse — it needs more certainty before calling something 'calm'.

params.name: Why this page exists
params.plain: It answers: can the grid edge survive the fastest, most expensive data?
params.why: Profit factor 0.96 — still slightly negative after fees. Timeframe matters as much as strategy.
